thesis: The gate's complexity is itself the largest operational risk, and the record proves it: 26 adversarial review rounds on PR #444 produced a close-audit criterion that embeds ~24 of its own findings as inline citations (#887, #894, #909, #922, #923, #925, #934, #938, #939, #941, #942, #952, #953, #964/#969, #995, #996, #997, #1014, #1015, #1031, #1080, #1081, #1082), grew open tech-debt from 289 to 754 in six days (~2.6x manufacture-vs-resolve, #980), rides on a fingerprint pipeline that is broken and mass-duplicating (#471/#688), and has shipped zero releases — the gate script has never executed even once, and two criteria are formally 'not evaluable' pending #511 and #649. Meanwhile the ONE real laundering incident on record — #120 falsely closed 'completed' for a week while its fix PR #311 sat unmerged — was healed by a single reopen API call, which none of the 280 lines of close-audit predicate would have caught because the gate only runs at release time. The bet: check OPEN state only with ~6 one-query criteria; delete close-auditing as pass/fail logic and replace it with a nightly detect-and-reopen auditor, because a reopened laundered close re-enters the open criteria the gate already checks. Detection-and-reopen dominates prevention-by-predicate: it protects every day (not just the release instant), it repairs the STATE so dashboards and /factory-status are right too (the #120 miscount hurt for a week precisely because state was wrong while any query-time archaeology would have left it wrong), it cannot false-red a release, it costs one nightly job instead of an unimplemented 1500-line GraphQL/hunk-parser/signature-verifier, and it stops feeding the review loop that is manufacturing the very backlog the gate counts.
design: THE GATE IS EXACTLY SIX CRITERIA, all over CURRENT state, each one fully-paginated search query (the same query shape /factory-status already runs; #419/#420 pagination fixes are prerequisites). Criterion 1: zero open issues labeled `bug`. Criterion 2: zero open issues labeled `tech-debt` that carry `P0` or `P1` (most-severe governs if multiple). Criterion 3: zero open issues labeled `security`, any type, any priority (ADR 0005's cross-priority security precedence, kept). Criterion 4: zero open `tech-debt` issues lacking a `P0`-`P3` label — fail-closed on untriaged; legacy `priority:*`/`high`/`medium`/`low` labels do not count (#510 clears this). Criterion 5: zero open issues labeled `gate:confirmed-high` (clerk applies at filing time; the label is a severity floor coexisting with P-labels). Criterion 6: mechanical artifact checks — coverage >=95% lines on `hooks/scripts/**` and `hooks/lib/common.sh` at the exact SHA /ship builds; 3 consecutive green `nightly-eval.yml` runs on main (thresholds per #511); the `docs/PRODUCT.md` feature-freeze marker line reads ON; prerequisite issues #419, #420, #510, #511 closed and the close-auditor deployed with >=1 successful run (replacing #649's ceremony — see migration); zero unresolved `.factory/review` findings; every v1.0.0 roadmap item merged-green except M4's two terminal boxes (#527 carve-out, kept).

CLOSE-AUDITING IS A NIGHTLY REPORT-AND-REPAIR JOB, NOT A GATE PREDICATE. A new `close-audit.yml` nightly workflow runs `hooks/scripts/close-audit.sh` (fixture-tested, inside the 95% coverage floor): it scans closes since its last run (since the 2026-07-29 baseline on first run) of issues that carry or ever carried `bug`/`tech-debt`/`security`/`gate:confirmed-high` — timeline queries are FINE here because this is a report, not a pass/fail predicate — and applies cheap repair heuristics: (a) gate-relevant issue closed `not planned` -> reopen with a comment; (b) closed `completed` with no merged closing PR and no default-branch commit naming the issue -> reopen + `needs-triage`; (c) closed `duplicate` whose most-recent duplicate target is not itself open-and-gate-relevant or legitimately closed -> reopen; (d) `security`/`gate:confirmed-high`/`tech-debt`/`bug` label removed from an open issue with no closing fix -> re-apply the label with a comment. A reopened issue lands back in criteria 1-5 (untriaged reopens block via criterion 4; reopened bugs block via criterion 1), so laundering is self-healing: worst case is a false-green window bounded by one nightly cycle, and the release report (below) shows every close since baseline anyway.

REOPEN IS ONCE-PER-CLOSE-EVENT, NEVER A WAR. The auditor never reopens the same issue twice for the same close event; a re-closed issue's second close goes into the report's 'contested closes' section for the human release sign-off instead. This kills the reopen-loop failure mode without adding a predicate.

THE HUMAN WITNESS IS EXACTLY ONE SIGNATURE PER RELEASE, NOT PER EXEMPTION. The Release Gate script emits `gate-report.json` (canonical JSON, SHA-256 printed) containing: the six criteria results with counts, every P0/P1 -> P2/P3 down-rank since the 2026-07-29 baseline (down-rank visibility kept, as report content), the latest nightly close-audit summary including all contested closes and every close of a `security`/`gate:confirmed-high` issue since baseline, and any mass-close events. The gate FAILS unless `factory-ops/release/<version>/gate.ack` exists on the release branch containing that exact digest as its only line, in a commit whose VERIFIED signature (`signature.signer.login`, state VALID, author == committer == signer) resolves to an account listed under 'Human maintainers' in `MAINTAINERS.md` — fail-closed on unknown/unverified/mismatched identity. This keeps the one genuinely load-bearing trust mechanism (a human who cannot be spoofed by a settable email, per the #1080 finding) and deletes the per-exemption two-principal branching, the release-captain's self-acknowledgment hash field (an agent acking its own report adds zero trust), and every same-PR/different-PR/source-pr conditional.

FINGERPRINT, LOCATION, HUNK-WINDOW, AND SOURCE-PR DATA BECOME ADVISORY REPORT CONTENT. The auditor includes, per audited close, whatever binding evidence exists (closing PR link, fingerprint citation in the squash commit, diff-touches-location) as report annotations to help the human judge contested closes in seconds — but none of it is pass/fail logic. This is the correct trust posture while the fingerprint pipeline itself is the repo's most-duplicated open bug (#471/#688): a broken de-dup cannot be a load-bearing anti-laundering anchor, and #471/#688 get fixed on their own P0 track for de-dup, not for gating.

ONE SPEC SECTION, ~40 LINES, IMPLEMENTABLE THIS SPRINT. The six criteria replace the current ~280-line section in `docs/specs/epic-1/spec.md`. The gate script is ~150 lines of bash over the search API plus file checks — the same primitives /factory-status uses — testable to the 95% floor, versus the current design's unstarted requirement for LabeledEvent/UnlabeledEvent interval algebra, MarkedAsDuplicateEvent chain traversal with cycle detection, closedByPullRequestsReferences joins, old-file-coordinate hunk-window parsing, and three-way signature identity resolution. Every criterion is decidable by an operator reading it once, which is the property 26 review rounds proved the current text does not have: each mechanism patch spawned the next round's findings against the patch.
kept_mechanisms: Fail-closed on untriaged tech-debt (criterion 4) — ADR 0005's core scope decision, unchanged
Security precedence across all priority levels (criterion 3) — ADR 0005, unchanged
`gate:confirmed-high` as a clerk-applied severity floor on open issues (criterion 5), with the auditor re-applying it if stripped
Fully-paginated counting everywhere; #419/#420 as hard prerequisites
Coverage floor widened to `hooks/lib/common.sh`, measured at the /ship SHA (ADR 0005)
3 consecutive green nightly evals; #511 threshold ownership by qa
#527's self-reference carve-out for M4's two terminal roadmap boxes
Down-rank visibility since the 2026-07-29 baseline — demoted from gate-embedded prose to gate-report content
Verified-signature human maintainer binding (the #1080 signer-not-email rule) — kept, but exercised exactly once per release
Canonical-JSON gate report with SHA-256 content hash
cut_mechanisms: Ever-carried timeline set membership in gate predicates (#887) — replaced by nightly label-repair: fix the state once instead of re-deriving history on every query, which also fixes every dashboard the timeline query would have left wrong

The entire close-laundering criterion with exemptions (a)/(b) — deleted as pass/fail; its intent survives as auditor heuristics plus report content, and a reopened laundered close is already caught by criteria 1-5

Fingerprint-citation-in-immutable-squash-commit binding (#941) — cannot be load-bearing while the fingerprint pipeline is the repo's most-duplicated broken subsystem (#471/#688); demoted to report annotation

Hunk-overlap +/-20 old-file-coordinate location binding (#923/#942/#997/#1031) — took four review rounds to define, admits cosmetic near-line edits by its own 'residual risk' text, and requires a diff parser nobody has built; demoted to report annotation

source-pr same-PR/different-PR exemption logic (#995/#1082) — self-certification is handled by the one human signature that reads the report, not by a conditional that itself needed a #1082 patch to avoid permanent false-red

Per-exemption two-principal witness (#996/#1014/#1015/#1080/#1081) — collapsed to one human signature per release; five findings' worth of identity-plumbing for a ceremony that fires per-exemption is the god-spec signature

Duplicate-chain transitive resolution with floor inheritance (#939) — replaced by the auditor's one-hop check (terminal target open-and-gate-relevant or reopen), with chains surfacing as contested closes in the report
gateReportHash self-acknowledgment in `.factory/state/release-intent.json` (#934/#938/#952) — an agent acknowledging its own artifact adds no trust; the human ack file is the only acknowledgment

#649 as a standalone backfill-audit prerequisite — rescoped into the auditor's bootstrap run (first run backfills `gate:confirmed-high` labels and normalizes what it can, reports the rest); a separate audit-record ceremony blocking criterion evaluability is deleted
The 'not evaluable until X closes' meta-states — a gate criterion that cannot be evaluated is a spec bug, not a feature; under this design every criterion is evaluable on day one
migration: PR #444 lands in three moves, all smaller than what it currently carries. (1) Freeze the adversarial re-review loop on #444 now (the sprint-4 plan already directs this; the loop is the damage). (2) #444 shrinks to docs-only: replace `docs/specs/epic-1/spec.md` section 'Release Gate for v1.0.0' with the six-criteria text (~40 lines for ~280); ADR 0005's scope decisions (fail-closed triage, security precedence, M5 deferral home, coverage widening) stand unchanged — the panel's synthesis ADR supersedes only its close-audit/consequences machinery; `docs/PRODUCT.md` keeps rationale and points at the spec. This makes #444 mergeable in one round because there is almost no predicate text left to attack. (3) A separate small implementation PR adds `close-audit.yml` + `hooks/scripts/close-audit.sh` with fixture tests under the coverage floor, and the Release Gate script gains its six checks. The ~two dozen open findings filed against the now-deleted spec machinery are closed referencing the synthesis ADR — and, deliberately, that mass-close appears in the auditor's first report for the human to witness at the next release sign-off: the migration eats its own dogfood instead of exempting itself (the self-exemption ADR 0005 already forbids, #964/#969). #471/#688 remain P0 on their own merits (de-dup and the debt-reconcile Stop hook), decoupled from gate evaluability.
risks_accepted: A laundered close can be false-green for up to one nightly cycle (~24h) before detect-and-reopen fires. Bounded, and the release report lists every close since baseline for the signing human regardless; /ship MAY run the auditor as a courtesy pre-step, but that is hygiene, not a predicate.

A determined agent can launder via a merged, non-empty-diff, plausibly-linked PR that fixes nothing; heuristics will not catch it and the signing human is the backstop. Accepted openly because the current design admits the same by its own text ('a near-line cosmetic edit can still technically satisfy the intersection') at ~100x the mechanism cost.
Stripping a `security` or floor label from an open issue exits criteria 3/5 until the nightly re-applies it — same bounded window, and the strip event is named in the report.

A P0->P1... P2 down-rank of non-security, non-floored debt exits criterion 2 with report-only visibility, no predicate brake. Accepted: re-ranking is an authorized product-owner act (ADR 0005 says so), and the human signature is the review point.

An adversary who re-closes after the one permitted reopen wins until release sign-off, where the contested-closes section surfaces it; between nightlies and sign-off there is no third automated defense. Accepted to prevent reopen wars.

The one human becomes a single point of judgment once per release. That is the point: one accountable, unspoofable signature over one readable report, instead of judgment smuggled into two dozen predicates that 26 rounds could not stabilize.
